subject: Design review: keystore shielding, BYOK attestation flow, and egress groups

Subject: Intro: BYOK needs for Nebula private deployment

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the time earlier. As promised, attaching the high level asks from our infra/security team around BYOK for our private VPC deployment of Redwood:

- We need a review of the attestation flow when customer-supplied keys are wrapped and imported into the HSM.
- Clear network separation for the keystore operator plane (no internet egress allowed, except limited attestation endpoints).
- An egress group matrix that maps which Redwood control plane endpoints can be reached and why.
- Rotation guidance that supports offline key rotation ceremonies and retains auditability for SOC2.

We've pulled a few docs together on our side. Could your team propose an architecture that minimizes operator blast radius and shows how attestation to an external CA (or ACME's own attestation service) would look?

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-15T09:20:00Z
Subject: Internal: pre-read notes for Nebula BYOK review

Folks — quick notes ahead of Friday's call. I sketched the end-to-end we should present and the mitigations for operator risk. See attachments and callouts below.

1) Keystore shielding model (see keystore-shielding-arch.png)
   - HSM sits in customer VPC private subnet with no IGW.
   - Operator plane (keyboard/agent, key import services) live in a separate management subnet reachable only over a dedicated management peering + strict firewall rules.
   - All operator actions require short-lived operator certs (mTLS) and an operator session audit log forwarded (push-only) to customer SIEM — no operator shell persistence on the host.

2) Attestation flow options
   - Option A: Customer CA-based attestation — Redwood provides an attestation broker to translate TPM/Evidentiary attestation into a signed receipt that maps to a key import ID. Customer retains the private attestation root.
   - Option B: Remote attestation to Redwood's attestation service for a short-lived import token; token is audited and then immediately deleted.

Risks & mitigations:
   - Risk: Operator misbinding (operator could import key into wrong tenant). Mitigation: multi-actor approval + HSM policy requiring 'origin' assertion from attestation token.
   - Risk: Egress leakage from management subnet. Mitigation: egress group whitelist + DNS over private resolver + no public key-material uploads except to attestation endpoints. (See egress-groups-reference.csv)

3) Rotation + ceremonies
   - Support both online rotation (Redwood-managed wrap/unwrap flows) and offline ceremony (customer supplies wrapped blob, operator runs sealed import with 2-of-3 operator signoffs).
   - We will produce a rotation manifest (JSON) that is signed and uploaded to the customer's audit bucket as evidence.

4) Compliance framing
   - Keep canonical audit artifacts: attestation receipt, operator session logs, rotation manifest, signed consumption attestations (hashes). Retention policy should be configurable per customer SLA.

Open asks for Friday:
   - Nebula: do you have a dedicated CA for attestation? Who is the canonical audit bucket owner?
   - EdgeCloud: which control plane endpoints will you expect us to call during import?

Thanks — Mina
Security PM, Redwood Inference
Attachments referenced: byok-attestation-checklist.pdf, egress-groups-reference.csv
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.ai, hiro_tanaka@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-16T17:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Design review: keystore shielding, BYOK attestation flow, and egress groups — notes and decisions

Thanks everyone for a productive call. Notes and decisions below (short version). Full slide deck + checklist uploaded to the linked Drive folder.

Decisions:
- Attestation: Nebula will use Option A (customer CA). Redwood will run an attestation broker that verifies TPM evidence and returns a signed attestation receipt. The customer's CA will sign the attestation root and remain under Nebula control.
- Operator plane isolation: management subnet + dedicated VPC peering. No direct internet egress from HSM subnet; operator tools run from management subnet with strict egress groups limited to: attestation broker, STS token exchange, and SIEM endpoints.
- Rotation: support both flows. For offline ceremonies, 2-of-3 operator signoff required before import. Rotation manifests must be uploaded to Nebula's audit bucket and signed by the Redwood rotation service.

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Action 1: Redwood to produce a documented attestation API contract (Mina) — due 2026-09-21.
- Action 2: Network egress whitelist (EdgeCloud + Redwood ops) — draft due 2026-09-18 (EdgeCloud to confirm list).
- Action 3: Rotation manifest schema + example (Hiro) — due 2026-09-20.
- Action 4: Preflight runbook and operator checklist (Monica) — due 2026-09-22.

Open questions captured:
- How long will the attestation broker retain evidence before deletion? (Tom requested short retention with proof-of-deletion).
- Customer desire to use a hardware-backed CA vs. software CA for root signing — need Nebula to confirm.

Attachments: keystore-shielding-arch.png, byok-attestation-checklist.pdf (uploaded to Drive)

— Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@nebulahealth.com>

Subject: Re: Design review: keystore shielding, BYOK attestation flow, and egress groups — ack and next steps

Vanessa / team — solid session, thanks. Nebula confirms:
- We will provide a hardware-backed CA for attestation root and expect attestation receipts to be issued against that root.
- For evidence retention, Nebula requires a proof-of-deletion record: Redwood should provide a signed digest of retained evidence plus a deletion timestamp and signed deletion confirmation once evidence is purged.

We'll review the attestation API contract when Mina sends it. Friday's notes look good — Tom

Tom Reyes
Head of Infrastructure, Nebula Health Systems
